household.name: pelt-stretcher
household.title: pelt-stretcher
household.reason: A wooden lynx pelt-stretcher, a traditional hunting/household tool used by Dene peoples like the Tłı̨chǫ (Dogrib) for processing furs, consistent with their subarctic trapping economy.

household.name: head-band; tumpline
household.title: head-band; tumpline
household.reason: A padded hide/cotton tumpline with cordage ends, used to strap loads across the forehead — a classic Dene/Dogrib (Tłı̨chǫ) carrying device, matching the museum's own attribution to the Dogrib.

garment.name: moccasin
garment.title: moccasin
garment.reason: A pair of smoked moosehide moccasins with beaver fur trim and floral glass beadwork, directly attributed by the museum to Dogrib (Tłı̨chǫ) makers — a well-documented Dene craft form.

garment.name: parka
garment.title: parka
garment.reason: This is a classic Dene-style child's parka with smoke-tanned hide fringed yoke, floral beadwork, and fur trim at hood, cuffs and hem — a garment type made and worn by Dene peoples including the Tłı̨chǫ (Dogrib), matching the museum's own attribution.

garment.name: slipper
garment.title: slipper
garment.reason: Pair of moose-skin slippers with porcupine quillwork and beaver fur trim, directly attributed by the museum to the Dogrib (Tłı̨chǫ) people, a well-documented Dene craft.
